chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Salama ibn al-Khattab, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Mu'adab, from Asim ibn Hamid, from Khalid al-Qalanisi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The old man is brought on the Day of Resurrection and his Record is handed to him with the side facing the people showing his sins, and only his evil deeds are seen, so that feels long to him. He says: 'O my Lord, do You order me to the Fire?' The Almighty says: 'O old man, I feel shy to punish you, since you prayed to Me in the world. Take My servant to Paradise!'
ai.seo_question: Why does God forgive the sins of an old man on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this narration highlights the virtue of longevity and the intercessory power of consistent prayer (*salat*), illustrating how divine modesty (*istihya*) can override the prominence of recorded sins for the elderly. It reflects the Shia emphasis on the spiritual maturity and accumulated worship of those who live long lives, serving as a comfort to believers who fear their shortcomings.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 22-26 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Salamat ibn al-Khat’tab, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein , on the authority of Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Mo’adab, on the authority of Asim ibn Hamid, on the authority of Khalid al-Qalanesi that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“When they bring an old man on the Resurrection Day for Reckoning, and hand him his Record of Deeds with the side of it showing his sins and evil deeds facing the people, time will pass very slowly for him. He will say, ‘O my Lord! Do you order that I be taken to Hell?’ God - may His Majesty be Exalted - says, ‘O old man! I feel too shy to punish you, since you prayed when you were living in the world. Take My servant to Paradise!’”
